ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is an upper semicircle with FE as the diameter, F, D, A, E are on the same horizontal diameter line, and FD=9, DA=16, AE=9 are marked. The bottom side of rectangle ABCD is DA, the vertical sides DC and AB go upward, and vertices C, B are located on the semicircular arc. Reasoning: FE=FD+DA+AE=9+16+9=34, so the radius of the circle where the semicircle is located is 17. Since the left and right gaps FD and AE are both 9, the center of the circle is located directly below the midpoint of DA; DA=16, so the horizontal distance from the center of the circle to A or D is 8. Let the height of the rectangle be h, then vertex B (or C) is on the circle, satisfying h^2+8^2=17^2. Calculating gives h^2=289-64=225, so h=15. The area of the rectangle is DA·h=16×15=240.

method.method_draft: Use a coordinate/circle-equation setup. From the image, read that F, D, A, E are collinear on the diameter FE, the rectangle has base DA along the diameter, and the top vertices C and B lie on the semicircle. From the text, use DA=16 and FD=AE=9, so FE=9+16+9=34 and the semicircle radius is 17. Because the side gaps are equal, the center of the circle is directly under the midpoint of DA. Thus each vertical side of the rectangle is 8 units horizontally from the center. Let the rectangle height be h. A top corner such as B lies on the circle, so h^2+8^2=17^2. Solve h=15, then area=16·15=240.

method.method_draft: Use the right-triangle altitude theorem inside the semicircle. From the image, note that C lies on the semicircle with FE as diameter, and CD is perpendicular to FE because CD is a vertical side of rectangle ABCD. From the text, FD=9, DA=16, and AE=9, so DE=DA+AE=25. Since C is on the semicircle with diameter FE, triangle FCE is right at C by Thales' theorem. Segment CD is the altitude from the right angle to the hypotenuse FE, so CD^2=FD·DE=9·25=225. Therefore CD=15. The rectangle has base DA=16 and height CD=15, so its area is 240.
